title: Sawin’s totally real towers
summary: The library constructs totally real number fields of arbitrarily large degree while keeping their root discriminants bounded and the same infinite set of primes completely split.
overview: The main theorem constructs totally real number fields of arbitrarily large degree with root discriminant at most 255255. One fixed infinite set of rational primes, all congruent to one modulo four, splits completely in every field. The degree can therefore grow while both the discriminant bound and the splitting conditions remain fixed.

The construction starts with the maximal totally real pro-2 extension of the rationals unramified outside six odd primes. Carefully chosen Frobenius relations force primes to split, while a Golod–Shafarevich estimate keeps the resulting quotient infinite. Its finite layers provide fields of large degree, and restricted ramification controls their discriminants. These results formalize the arithmetic tower used in Sawin’s unit-distance work.
scopeNote: This guide covers ten concrete definitions and results from the public repository, not a formalization of the entire unit-distance disproof. The main endpoint is an arithmetic existence theorem. Its proof supplies the bound 255255 without claiming optimality. The separately listed Shafarevich theorem assumes an odd prime and must not be substituted for the pro-2 arithmetic used in the tower construction.

entries.title: The maximal real pro-p extension with restricted ramification
entries.summary: The ambient arithmetic extension is built from its admissible finite Galois layers.
statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a set $T$ of finite places of $\mathbb Q$. A finite Galois intermediate field $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is admissible when $\operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbb Q)$ is a $p$-group, $E/\mathbb Q$ is unramified at finite places outside $T$, and it is unramified at infinite places.

The extension is defined inside a fixed algebraic closure by $$M_{p,T}=\bigvee_{\text{admissible }E}E.$$ Over $\mathbb Q$, the infinite-place condition says that the finite layer is totally real. The Lean definition allows a natural-number parameter; the prime case is the intended pro-$p$ application.
discussion: The maximal totally real pro-p extension unramified outside a chosen set of primes is built by taking the compositum of all finite Galois extensions with those properties. This keeps finite portions of the extension accessible through finite Galois theory. Requiring total reality is especially important at p equal to two, since control of finite ramification alone does not ensure it.
history: Shafarevich’s 1963 work studies extensions with prescribed ramification. Golod and Shafarevich’s 1964 paper then showed that class field towers can be infinite. Maximal pro-p extensions with restricted ramification are the natural setting in which those arithmetic constraints can be combined with generator–relation criteria for infinitude.

entries.title: Which finite fields lie in the maximal extension?
entries.summary: Admissibility is equivalent to containment in the constructed maximal extension.
statement: Write $M_{p,T}$ for the compositum in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of the finite Galois extensions that are totally real, unramified outside $T$, and have $p$-group Galois group. For prime $p$, this is the maximal totally real pro-$p$ extension unramified outside $T$.

Let $T$ be a set of finite places of $\mathbb Q$, and let $E$ be a finite Galois intermediate field of $\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q$. Then $$E\subseteq M_{p,T}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E\text{ is an admissible finite layer for }(p,T).$$

Admissibility means a $p$-group Galois group, no finite ramification outside $T$, and no infinite-place ramification. The declaration is stated for a natural-number parameter $p$; its later uses take $p$ prime. The finite Galois hypothesis on $E$ is part of the statement.
discussion: A finite Galois field lies in the constructed maximal extension exactly when it satisfies the prescribed p-group, ramification, and total-reality conditions. Containment therefore recovers the arithmetic information needed to study a finite layer. This is useful when choosing fields of large degree inside an infinite extension: one can establish their containment and then obtain the conditions needed for discriminant and splitting arguments.
history: Profinite Galois theory organizes infinite Galois extensions through their finite layers and finite quotient groups. Ribes and Zalesskii give the group-theoretic framework, while Shafarevich’s prescribed-ramification work supplies the arithmetic setting. Here the finite-layer characterization connects those viewpoints without assuming an independent description of the infinite extension.

entries.title: Five generators for the initial arithmetic group
entries.summary: The maximal real pro-2 group for the six chosen ramified primes has generator rank exactly five.
statement: Let $$S=\{3,5,7,11,13,17\},\qquad M=M_{2,S},\qquad G=\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb Q),$$ where $S$ is viewed as the corresponding finite places. The theorem proves both that $G$ can be topologically generated by at most five elements and that its topological generator rank is exactly five. Here $M_{2,S}$ is the maximal totally real pro-$2$ extension of $\mathbb Q$ unramified at finite primes outside $S$.

The generator count is for the actual Galois group of the maximal real extension unramified outside $S$. It is not an assumed parameter of an abstract pro-$2$ group. In particular, ramification at $2$ is excluded by this support.
discussion: The Galois group of the maximal totally real pro-2 extension unramified outside the six specified odd primes needs exactly five topological generators. Its Frattini quotient has order thirty-two, giving dimension five over the field with two elements and detecting the minimal generator count. This supplies the generator term in the Golod–Shafarevich estimate that will keep the arithmetic tower infinite.
history: Frattini quotients are a standard tool for determining generators of pro-p groups, as developed in Ribes and Zalesskii. The six-prime support used here also appears in Proposition 2.3 of Remarks. Its arithmetic is suited to obtaining a favorable balance between generators and relations.

entries.title: A five-generator presentation with at most six relations
entries.summary: The initial arithmetic group admits an actual finite minimal pro-2 presentation.
statement: Here $M_{2,S}$ denotes the maximal totally real pro-$2$ extension of $\mathbb Q$ unramified at finite primes outside $S$.

For $G=\operatorname{Gal}(M_{2,S}/\mathbb Q)$ with $S=\{3,5,7,11,13,17\}$, there exist a free pro-$2$ source, a natural number $r\le6$, and an actual presentation $$G\cong F_5/\overline{\langle\!\langle\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_r\rangle\!\rangle}$$ that is minimal on its five generators.

The formal object includes the continuous surjection and the displayed relators presenting its kernel. Minimality gives Zassenhaus depth at least two for these relators. The theorem says at most six relations, not exactly six.
discussion: The initial arithmetic Galois group has a minimal pro-2 presentation with five generators and at most six relations. This leaves room to impose further splitting conditions: at $t=5/12$, the bound $1-5t+6t^2=-1/24$ is strictly negative. Minimality puts the existing relators at depth at least two, while sufficiently deep additional relations contribute less than the remaining margin.
history: The generator–relation method comes from Golod and Shafarevich’s class field tower argument. Later cutting methods use a strict negative margin to impose new arithmetic conditions. The real pro-2 construction with this six-prime support appears in Remarks; the presentation supplies the numerical starting point for that strategy.

entries.title: Primes with deep Frobenius lifts
entries.summary: Arithmetic Frobenius elements can be lifted to successively deeper levels of one free pro-2 presentation.
statement: Put $S=\{3,5,7,11,13,17\}$ and $G=\operatorname{Gal}(M_{2,S}/\mathbb Q)$, where $M_{2,S}$ is the maximal totally real pro-$2$ extension of $\mathbb Q$ unramified at finite primes outside $S$.

There exist a five-generator minimal presentation $P:F_5\twoheadrightarrow G$ with at most six relators, primes $q_n$ and elements $f_n\in F_5$ such that $$q_n>n,\quad q_n\notin S,\quad q_n\equiv1\pmod4,\quad P(f_n)=\operatorname{Frob}_{q_n},\quad f_n\in D_{n+5}(F_5).$$ Here $D_k$ is the pro-$2$ Zassenhaus filtration.

The Frobenius elements are the arithmetic elements supplied by the source’s decomposition-group construction. The theorem chooses a presentation together with the sequence; the depth condition is imposed on lifts in that very free source.
discussion: Infinitely many primes congruent to one modulo four can be selected so that their arithmetic Frobenius elements have successively deeper lifts in one free pro-2 presentation. Chebotarev supplies the primes, and their increasing Zassenhaus depths make the cost of imposing the corresponding relations summable. The bound that the nth selected prime exceeds n ensures an infinite set without requiring the sequence to be strictly increasing.
history: Hajir, Maire, and Ramakrishna’s Cutting towers of number fields develops the refined Golod–Shafarevich method for imposing splitting conditions. Proposition 2.3 of Remarks adapts the Chebotarev selection by adjoining fourth roots of unity, obtaining primes congruent to one modulo four. The deep lifts connect that selection with the relation budget.

entries.title: Killing infinitely many Frobenius elements without making the group finite
entries.summary: There is an infinite quotient in which the selected primes have trivial decomposition groups.
statement: Let $G=\operatorname{Gal}(M_{2,S}/\mathbb Q)$ with $S=\{3,5,7,11,13,17\}$, where $M_{2,S}$ is the maximal totally real pro-$2$ extension of $\mathbb Q$ unramified at finite primes outside $S$. There is a sequence of primes $q_n>n$, outside $S$ and congruent to one modulo four, with infinite range, for which $$G/\overline{\langle\!\langle\operatorname{Frob}_{q_n}:n\ge0\rangle\!\rangle}$$ is infinite.

The accompanying decomposition-group theorem states that the image of the entire decomposition group at each selected prime is trivial in this quotient. This is the group-theoretic condition that will force complete splitting in the corresponding fixed field.
discussion: One can kill infinitely many selected Frobenius elements in the initial arithmetic Galois group so that the resulting quotient remains infinite. At $t=5/12$, their total contribution is bounded by $\sum_{n\ge0}t^{n+5}=t^5/(1-t)<1/24$, within the initial presentation’s negative margin. A limiting argument imposes all the relations together. The selected primes then split completely in the fixed field, whose infinite Galois group provides finite layers of unbounded degree.
history: Hajir, Maire, and Ramakrishna’s 2019 preprint constructs infinite extensions with bounded ramification using refined Golod–Shafarevich estimates. It also obtains infinitely many completely split primes. Frobenius cutting is the key mechanism: additional splitting relations are chosen deep enough that the resulting tower remains infinite.

entries.title: A uniform root-discriminant bound of 255255
entries.summary: Restricted tame ramification gives an exponential bound for the actual number-field discriminant.
statement: Let $L/\mathbb Q$ be a finite Galois number field whose Galois group is a $2$-group. Assume it is unramified at finite places outside $S=\{3,5,7,11,13,17\}$. Then $$|\operatorname{disc}(L)|\le255255^{[L:\mathbb Q]},\qquad255255=3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17.$$

Consequently its root discriminant satisfies $|\operatorname{disc}(L)|^{1/[L:\mathbb Q]}\le255255$. Total reality is not an assumption of this discriminant theorem; it is supplied separately when the theorem is applied to the chosen tower.
discussion: A finite Galois extension of the rationals with a 2-group Galois group and ramification confined to the six specified odd primes has root discriminant at most 255255. Ramification is tame, so each allowed prime’s discriminant exponent is bounded by the degree. Multiplying these bounds gives a constant that works uniformly through the tower, even as the degrees grow without bound.
history: Martinet’s 1978 paper connects class field towers with discriminant estimates. Hajir, Maire, and Ramakrishna later obtained new root-discriminant bounds through their cutting method. The constant here comes from the chosen six-prime support and is used as a uniform bound, rather than as a claim to an optimal numerical record.

entries.title: One infinite prime set splitting in fields of unbounded degree
entries.summary: A single infinite set of primes splits completely in totally real fields with uniformly bounded root discriminant.
statement: There are a real constant $B$ and an infinite set $Q$ of primes, all congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, such that for every $N$ there is a totally real number field $F$ with $$[F:\mathbb Q]\ge N,\qquad |\operatorname{disc}(F)|^{1/[F:\mathbb Q]}\le B,$$ and every $q\in Q$ splits completely in $F$.

The implementation chooses $B=255255$. Its explicit splitting conclusion supplies $[F:\mathbb Q]$ distinct maximal ideals of $\mathcal O_F$ containing $q$. For a rational prime in a number field, this maximal number of distinct primes above $q$ expresses complete splitting.
discussion: There are totally real number fields of arbitrarily large degree with uniformly bounded root discriminant in which the same infinite set of primes splits completely. The prime set is fixed before the degree threshold is chosen. This combines controlled discriminant growth with persistent splitting, providing arithmetic input for constructions using many conjugates and split primes, including the unit-distance application.
history: This infinite-prime formulation is Proposition 2.3 of the joint paper Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture. It uses the Frobenius-cutting method of Hajir, Maire, and Ramakrishna. Sawin’s single-author paper gives related arithmetic ingredients for the unit-distance application; its formulation and the joint paper’s proposition should be distinguished.

entries.title: A Martinet-type bounded-discriminant corollary
entries.summary: Forgetting the splitting conditions yields totally real number fields of unbounded degree and bounded root discriminant.
statement: There exists a real number $C>0$ such that for every natural number $N$ there are an integer $d\ge N$ and a totally real number field $K$ with $$[K:\mathbb Q]=d,\qquad|\operatorname{disc}(K)|\le C^d.$$

Thus one constant controls the discriminants exponentially in the degree, while the degrees are unbounded. Equivalently, the root discriminants of the chosen fields are uniformly bounded. The field may depend on $N$, but $C$ does not.
discussion: Totally real number fields can have arbitrarily large degree while their root discriminants remain bounded by one constant. This follows by discarding the prime-splitting conditions in the stronger tower theorem. It gives a family in which increasing degree does not force the root discriminant to grow, although the field may vary with the threshold and every exact degree is not prescribed.
history: Martinet’s 1978 Tours de corps de classes et estimations de discriminants is a primary source for the connection between class field towers and discriminant bounds. The corollary records that existence phenomenon for totally real fields. Here it follows from a theorem that additionally controls splitting of infinitely many primes.

entries.title: Shafarevich’s relation-rank bound for odd primes
entries.summary: Degree-two continuous cohomology of the maximal everywhere-unramified pro-p group is finite and arithmetically bounded.
statement: Let $F$ be a number field and $p$ an odd prime. Let $G$ be its maximal everywhere-unramified pro-$p$ Galois group, and let $d(G)$ be its finite topological generator rank. Write $r_1,r_2$ for its numbers of real and complex places and put $\delta=1$ if $F$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity, and $\delta=0$ otherwise.

The theorem proves that $H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\mathbb F_p)$ is finite-dimensional and $$\dim_{\mathbb F_p}H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\mathbb F_p)\le d(G)+(r_1+r_2-1)+\delta.$$ The coefficient module is the trivial module.
discussion: For an odd prime p, the degree-two continuous cohomology of the maximal everywhere-unramified pro-p Galois group is finite-dimensional and bounded by arithmetic data of the number field. The bound involves generator rank, unit rank, and a roots-of-unity correction. Because this cohomology controls relations, the estimate can combine with generator counts to prove infinitude; its odd-prime hypothesis excludes direct use in the separate pro-2 construction.
history: Shafarevich’s 1963 paper studies extensions with prescribed ramification and underlies the arithmetic relation estimates used in class field tower theory. Golod and Shafarevich’s subsequent infinitude argument shows why these bounds matter: controlling relations relative to generators can force an unramified tower to continue indefinitely.
